title: Compiling an exponential certificate language
statement: Let $L$ and $V$ be languages over the Boolean alphabet, and let $C,c,A,d$ be natural numbers. Suppose that for every Boolean word $x$, membership $x\in L$ is equivalent to the existence of a Boolean word $u$ with $|u|=C\,(2^{|x|+1})^c$ and $xu\in V$. Suppose also that a finite deterministic Turing machine $M$ decides $V$ within time $A(m+1)^d$ on inputs of length $m$. Then there exist natural numbers $K,r$ and a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ that decides $L$ within time $K\bigl(n+C(2^{n+1})^c+1\bigr)^r$.
hypotheses_covered: Languages $L$ and $V$ over the Boolean alphabet
Certificate characterization for every input word $x$
replaced: Let $L$ be a language over the binary alphabet such that $x \in L$ exactly when some binary string $u$ with $|u| = C \cdot 2^{(|x|+1)^c}$ has $x\,u \in V$, and let $M$ be a deterministic machine deciding the verifier language $V$ within $A(m+1)^d$. Then there are constants $K, r$ and a nondeterministic machine deciding $L$ within $K\,(n + C\cdot 2^{(n+1)^c} + 1)^r$.
